latest_release.name: v0.36.0
latest_release.body:
Thanks again to Michal (@akfaew) for another round of fixes in this release.

## Breaking changes — read before upgrading

> [!WARNING]
> **v0.36.0 includes breaking API, decoding, and serialization changes.**
>
> **Your code may fail to compile. Code that still compiles may decode or serialize
> differently. Events API URL-verification responses now use a different JSON key.**
>
> Review every item below before upgrading, including RTM and Events API handlers,
> tests that build or compare event payloads, and code that decodes into reused values.

### 1. RTM `group_rename` event types have changed

- **`slack.GroupRenameEvent` gains `EventTimestamp`.** Positional struct literals no
  longer compile. Use keyed literals, such as
  `slack.GroupRenameEvent{Type: "group_rename", Group: info, Timestamp: ts}`.
  `Timestamp` keeps its `ts` JSON key; the new `event_ts` key is omitted when empty.
- **`slack.GroupRenameInfo.Created` is now `int64`.** Replace `Created: "1360782804"`
  with `Created: 1360782804`. Parse input strings with `strconv.ParseInt(value, 10, 64)`,
  and use `strconv.FormatInt(info.Created, 10)` where a string is still needed.
  Marshaling now emits a JSON number, and decoding rejects quoted timestamps.

### 2. URL-verification responses use a lowercase `challenge` key

`slackevents.ChallengeResponse` now marshals as `{"challenge":"..."}` instead of
`{"Challenge":"..."}`, matching Slack's documented response. **Assignments from
untagged anonymous structs no longer compile;** use
`slackevents.ChallengeResponse{Challenge: value}` instead.

### 3. `slackevents.CallRejectedEvent` is flattened

- **Read fields directly from the event.** Replace `event.Event.CallID` with
  `event.CallID`, and likewise for `Type`, `UserID`, `ChannelID`, and `ExternalUniqueID`.
- **Envelope fields are removed.** `Token`, `TeamID`, `APIAppID`, `EventID`, and
  `AuthedUsers` are gone. Decode full callback payloads with `slackevents.ParseEvent`
  and read envelope metadata from the returned `EventsAPIEvent` and its
  `*EventsAPICallbackEvent` data.
- **`Type` is now `call_rejected`**, not the outer `event_callback`. Marshaling
  produces the inner event object instead of the complete callback envelope.

### 4. Decoding into reused values replaces previous contents

- **`ActionCallbacks`, `ContextElements`, and `BlockObjects` replace previous entries
  instead of appending.** Decoding `[A, B]` followed by `[C]` now leaves `[C]`; `[]` and
  JSON `null` clear all entries. The legacy `{"elements":null}` wrapper remains a no-op
  for `ContextElements`. To accumulate entries, decode separately and append the slices.
- **`Accessory` and `SlackResponseErrors` replace all previous variants** on a
  successful decode, instead of retaining fields from earlier decodes. JSON `null`
  clears accessory variants; it remains a no-op for `SlackResponseErrors` and for the
  legacy `{"accessory":null}` wrapper.

**A failed decode may clear or partially replace the destination.** Do not use it
after a decoding error. To keep the previous value, decode into a separate value and
assign it only after success.

## Added

- Add `AdminUsersSetAdmin`, `AdminUsersSetOwner`, and `AdminUsersSetRegular`, with
  `Context` variants, to change a user's account type on a workspace or Enterprise org.
  With an org ID, `admin.users.setRegular` also removes the user's Workspace Owner
  roles ([Slack changelog](https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2026/11/13/admin-users-set-regular-org-demotion)).
  The existing `SetRegular` still calls the legacy `users.admin.setRegular` endpoint.
- Add `AdminUsersGetExpiration` and `AdminUsersSetExpiration`, with `Context`
  variants, to read and set when a guest account is disabled.
  `AdminUsersGetExpirationOptionTargetTeam` and `AdminUsersSetExpirationOptionTeamID`
  select a workspace in the org. Slack API reference:
  [`admin.users.getExpiration`](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/admin.users.getExpiration),
  [`admin.users.setExpiration`

detail.readme:
Slack API in Go [![Go Reference](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/slack-go/slack.svg)](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/slack-go/slack) [![CI](https://github.com/slack-go/slack/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/slack-go/slack/actions/workflows/test.yml)
===============

You can chat with us on the [#slack-go](https://gophers.slack.com/archives/C02JQ98JHNC), [#slack-go-ja](https://gophers.slack.com/archives/C02HNL8EN3H) Slack channel on the [Gophers Slack](https://gophers.slack.com).

![logo](logo.png "icon")

This library supports most if not all of the `api.slack.com` REST
calls, as well as the Real-Time Messaging protocol over websocket, in
a fully managed way.

## Project Status
There is currently no major version released.
Therefore, minor version releases may include backward incompatible changes.

See [Releases](https://github.com/slack-go/slack/releases) for more information about the changes.

## Go Versions supported

We support the same versions of Go as the officially supported Go versions (see [Go
Release Policy](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#policy)).

## Installing

### *go get*

```bash
go get -u github.com/slack-go/slack
```

## Example

### Getting all groups

```golang
import (
    "fmt"

    "github.com/slack-go/slack"
)

func main() {
    api := slack.New("YOUR_TOKEN_HERE")
    // If you set debugging, it will log all requests to the console
    // Useful when encountering issues
    // slack.New("YOUR_TOKEN_HERE", slack.OptionDebug(true))
    groups, err := api.GetUserGroups(slack.GetUserGroupsOptionIncludeUsers(false))
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("%s\n", err)
        return
    }
    for _, group := range groups {
        fmt.Printf("ID: %s, Name: %s\n", group.ID, group.Name)
    }
}
```

### Getting User Information

```golang
import (
    "fmt"

    "github.com/slack-go/slack"
)

func main() {
    api := slack.New("YOUR_TOKEN_HERE")
    user, err := api.GetUserInfo("U023BECGF")
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("%s\n", err)
        return
    }
    fmt.Printf("ID: %s, Fullname: %s, Email: %s\n", user.ID, user.Profile.RealName, user.Profile.Email)
}
```

### HTTP retries

Retries are off by default. Use **OptionRetry(n)** for 429-only retries, or **OptionRetryConfig(cfg)** for full control (connection, 429, opt-in 5xx). With a custom client, pass retry options after `OptionHTTPClient`. See package `slack` doc for handler details.

```golang
api := slack.New("YOUR_TOKEN_HERE", slack.OptionRetry(3))
```

## Minimal Socket Mode usage:

See https://github.com/slack-go/slack/blob/master/examples/socketmode/socketmode.go


## Minimal RTM usage:

As mentioned in https://api.slack.com/rtm - for most applications, Socket Mode is a better way to communicate with Slack.

See https://github.com/slack-go/slack/blob/master/examples/websocket/websocket.go


## Minimal EventsAPI usage:

See https://github.com/slack-go/slack/blob/master/examples/eventsapi/events.go

## Socketmode Event Handler (Experimental)

When using socket mode, dealing with an event can be pretty lengthy as it requires you to route the event to the right place.

Instead, you can use `SocketmodeHandler` much like you use an HTTP handler to register which event you would like to listen to and what callback function will process that event when it occurs.

See [./examples/socketmode_handler/socketmode_handler.go](./examples/socketmode_handler/socketmode_handler.go)
## Contributing

You are more than welcome to contribute to this project.  Fork and
make a Pull Request, or create an Issue if you see any problem.

Before making any Pull Request please run the following:

```
make pr-prep
```

This will check/update code formatting, linting and then run all tests
